title: Release identity cannot be reconciled from the retrieved evidence
observation: The retrieved manifest identifies 74d6730e3832 / a12384067a75; newer verification references c1c67652e0b2 / fa69fa49e6d9 and a later candidate. Cached retrieval or deployment timing may explain this.
recommendation: Publish one immutable receipt linking commit, artifact digest, deployment ID, effective headers and test run. Re-fetch from a permitted browser before calling a release current.
acceptance: A fresh deployed manifest, independently computed runtime digest and CI receipt agree; historic records are labeled.

title: Capability statements differ across surfaced pages and source
observation: The fetched About copy says new calculations need local setup; the overview and current build source distinguish browser Terminal calculations. The build source already contains corrected About wording.
recommendation: Verify deployment and cache propagation; generate capability copy from a single versioned matrix and test all public descriptions.
acceptance: Overview, About, methodology, manifest and README make the same browser-versus-Python distinction.

title: Council protocol documentation needs versioned reconciliation
observation: AI_SETUP describes an earlier nine-role workflow with a 120-second timeout; CONNECTORS describes 17 or 25 model calls and a 300-second workflow. This may be version evolution, not a runtime defect.
recommendation: Identify the active protocol in the UI, docs and exports; deprecate old setup guidance; show consent, call-count and cost boundary before execution.
acceptance: One protocol ID resolves to the actual orchestration limits and explicit external-call status.

title: Public visual evidence spans different interface editions
observation: The homepage preview image shows an older Champion interface; newer candidate images show Terminal 2.0 with a different visual style. Neither proves the current deployed screen.
recommendation: Regenerate overview and sharing screenshots from the exact deployed build; include capture date and artifact revision.
acceptance: Homepage, social image and release gallery match the deployment receipt at desktop and mobile widths.

title: Protect model boundaries at result and export level
observation: Several models share interface concepts but differ in horizon, assumptions and physical fidelity. Published limits are useful; their persistent runtime presentation was not tested.
recommendation: Add an inseparable model card to results/exports: engine ID, synthetic/observed status, applicability, horizon, units, SOC policy, limitations and source revision.
acceptance: No numeric result can be copied, compared or exported without its model and data provenance.

title: Make the first useful experiment easier to reach on mobile
observation: The 390px published image spends its first 1000 vertical pixels on navigation, disclaimers, toolbars and introductory counts before substantive model controls.
recommendation: Offer task-led entry: explore an example, run the browser model, or use advanced local studies. Preserve visible limits but collapse repeated introductory copy.
acceptance: Usability sessions show users can identify mode and complete the first valid task without coaching.

title: Collect independent field and constrained-device performance evidence
observation: Published desktop lab timing is not field performance; the current audit could not run measurements. A large bundled runtime makes cold-start/parse costs worth testing.
recommendation: Measure cold/warm loads and interactions on real mid-range phones and constrained connections; split the hosted shell from optional datasets while retaining an offline edition.
acceptance: Report LCP, INP and CLS at mobile/desktop p75 when field volume permits; preserve raw runs and failures.

title: Complete assistive-technology and native-device acceptance
observation: Published automation is useful but explicitly does not establish screen-reader output, physical iOS behavior or full WCAG conformance.
recommendation: Test keyboard, VoiceOver/Safari and NVDA/Firefox or Chrome; include actual zoom/text scaling, tables, canvas alternatives and local scroll regions.
acceptance: Core journeys are operable and understandable; focus and announcements verified manually; exceptions documented.

title: Verify deployed SEO and crawler controls without undoing noindex
observation: Source defines metadata and a three-page sitemap. Direct robots/sitemap retrieval was unavailable; the audit did not observe effective headers or Search Console.
recommendation: Check source-generated output against deployed responses; retain runtime noindex for synthetic records; publish useful indexable lesson/model pages instead.
acceptance: Canonical, robots, status, sitemap, structured data and rendered visible text agree for each intended indexable page.

title: Version the public evidence and model documentation
observation: The methodology links retained-model references while the roadmap describes additional studies. Readers need a clear model-specific route rather than a global capability inference.
recommendation: Build a model registry with IDs, versions, equations, fixtures, validation tier and changelog; label historical quality reports and link the current receipt first.
acceptance: Each workspace and result links to exactly the applicable contract and validation evidence.

title: Preserve local state safely across updates and origins
observation: Local-only persistence is disclosed. Migration, quota failure, malformed imports and recovery were not exercised in this audit.
recommendation: Validate schemas, provide preview-before-import, migration receipts, recoverable backups and explicit overwrite/reset confirmation.
acceptance: Old/corrupt imports fail without silent data loss; export/import round trips preserve versioned fields.

title: Keep hashes, signatures and approval claims separate
observation: A digest can identify content and a signature can support key-possession evidence; neither alone proves scientific truth, signer authority or operational approval.
recommendation: Label each evidence claim by what it proves; retain raw inputs, verification status and human reviewer identity separately.
acceptance: No interface or export uses a hash/signature badge as a proxy for calibration, accreditation or approval.

title: Build discoverable, original learning and model pages
observation: The main intended indexable site is compact. The runtime is intentionally excluded from search, limiting discovery paths into its individual learning value.
recommendation: Publish reviewed HTML lessons, reproducible examples, a model glossary and capability comparisons with authorship and revision history. Avoid thin pages for every matrix cell.
acceptance: Pages answer genuine questions with unique evidence, internal links, accurate metadata and matching visible/schema facts.

title: Maintain a release-bound, risk-weighted test ledger
observation: A long feature list and large test count do not show which exact behaviors and combinations were exercised on the deployed artifact.
recommendation: Use the supplied catalogue and pairwise plans as traceable inputs; add stateful sequences and high-risk higher-order checks; attach evidence to each executed case.
acceptance: Every claim has an owner, artifact ID, expected outcome, actual status and screenshot/log; unknown is never counted as pass.
